components.text: Water never leaves Earth. It moves endlessly between oceans, air and land in a loop called the water cycle. This lesson covers three core processes, works through one example, and ends with a short self-check.

The sun heats water at the surface of oceans, lakes and rivers. Fast-moving molecules break free as water vapour and rise into the air. Plants also release vapour through their leaves, a process called transpiration.
As warm vapour rises it cools and turns back into tiny droplets around dust and salt particles, forming clouds. When droplets grow heavy enough they fall as precipitation: rain, snow, sleet or hail.
Precipitation gathers in rivers, lakes, groundwater and glaciers. Water flows downhill as runoff or soaks into the ground, eventually reaching the sea, where evaporation starts the cycle again.
Worked example: a puddle after rain
A 2 cm deep puddle forms after a storm. Follow what happens to its water over one sunny day.

items.label: Morning
items.text: Sunlight warms the puddle. Some water molecules gain enough energy to escape as vapour.

items.label: Midday
items.text: The puddle shrinks as evaporation speeds up. The vapour rises and cools in the air above.

items.label: Afternoon
items.text: Cooling vapour condenses into small clouds. No rain falls, so the vapour stays in the air.

items.label: Evening
items.text: The puddle is gone. Its water is now in the atmosphere, ready to fall again as precipitation.

components.title: Key idea
components.text: Water changes state but is never destroyed. The total amount of water on Earth stays roughly constant.

questions.question: Which process turns water vapour back into liquid droplets?
questions.explanation: Condensation happens when vapour cools and forms droplets, which build up into clouds.

questions.question: What is the main energy source that drives evaporation?
questions.explanation: Solar heating gives water molecules the energy they need to escape into the air.

questions.question: In the worked example, why did the puddle disappear without any rain?
questions.explanation: Evaporation moved the water from the puddle into the air as vapour.
